questions.question: What labels does rule_based_ner assign to ["Apple", "visited", "iPhone", "in", "US"]?
options: ["B-PERSON", "O", "B-ORG", "O", "B-ORG"]
["B-ORG", "O", "B-PRODUCT", "O", "B-GPE"]
["I-ORG", "O", "I-PRODUCT", "O", "I-GPE"]
questions.explanation: Apple, iPhone, and US are in the corresponding gazetteers; the other token is outside an entity.

questions.question: What shape string does word_shape("USA-2024") return?
options: Xxx-dddd
xxx-XXXX
XXX-dddd
questions.explanation: Uppercase letters become X, digits become d, and the hyphen is preserved.

questions.question: What BIO labels does spans_to_bio(["New","York","City"], [(0,3,"GPE")]) produce?
options: ["B-GPE", "I-GPE", "I-GPE"]
["B-GPE", "B-GPE", "B-GPE"]
["O", "B-GPE", "I-GPE"]
["GPE", "GPE", "GPE"]
questions.explanation: The span is half-open [0,3], so the first token gets B-GPE and the remaining two get I-GPE.

questions.question: What span tuple does bio_to_spans recover from B-ORG followed by I-ORG?
options: Two one-token spans, both labeled I-ORG
A tuple with the start, exclusive end, and label ORG
One span whose end is the start index
No span, because I-ORG can never follow B-ORG
questions.explanation: The function starts at B-ORG, extends the end for matching I-ORG labels, and emits (start, end, "ORG").

questions.question: What does bio_to_spans do when an I-PER token follows an active B-ORG span?
options: It silently changes the entire ORG span to PER
It appends I-PER to the ORG span
It closes the ORG span and does not extend it with the mismatched I-PER
It merges every entity until the next sentence
questions.explanation: The I branch extends only when the label type matches current[2]; otherwise the current span is emitted and cleared.

questions.question: What is a key limitation of rule_based_ner's gazetteer approach?
options: It always predicts nested entities with exact boundaries
It learns new entity types from unlabeled text during inference
It requires a dependency parser before checking any token
It cannot reliably disambiguate a name such as Apple from context when it is absent or used differently
questions.explanation: The rules check exact token membership in fixed sets, so unseen names and context-dependent meanings are missed.
